english: Let $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ be an invertible polynomial function with inverse function $f^{-1}$, such that $f(x)+2f^{-1}(x)=3x$ for all $x\in\mathbb{R}$ and $f(1)=7$. Then the value of $f(5)+f^{-1}(41)$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ एक व्युत्क्रमणीय बहुपद फलन है जिसका प्रतिलोम फलन $f^{-1}$ है, तथा सभी $x\in\mathbb{R}$ के लिए $f(x)+2f^{-1}(x)=3x$ है और $f(1)=7$ है। तब $f(5)+f^{-1}(41)$ का मान ______ है।
solution: Put $x=f(t)$ (allowed as $f$ is onto): $f(f(t))+2t=3f(t)$ for all $t$
If $\deg f=d$, then $\deg f(f(t))=d^{2}$ must equal $\max(d,1)$, so $d=1$: $f(t)=at+b$, $a\ne0$
solution_full: $f$ is invertible, so it is onto $\mathbb{R}$ and $f^{-1}(f(t))=t$ for every $t$. Putting $x=f(t)$ in the given relation: $f(f(t))+2t=3f(t)$ for all $t\in\mathbb{R}$.

Let $d=\deg f\ge1$ (a constant is not invertible). The left side has degree $d^{2}$ (the term $2t$ cannot cancel a degree $d^{2}\ge1$ term unless $d=1$), and the right side has degree $d$. So $d^{2}=d$, i.e. $d=1$, and $f(t)=at+b$ with $a\ne0$.
Then $f(f(t))=a(at+b)+b=a^{2}t+ab+b$, and the relation becomes $a^{2}t+ab+b+2t=3at+3b$ for all $t$. Comparing coefficients: $a^{2}-3a+2=0$, so $a=1$ or $a=2$; and $ab+b=3b$, i.e. $b(a-2)=0$.
If $a=1$, then $b=0$ and $f(x)=x$, which gives $f(1)=1\ne7$. So $a=2$, $b$ is free from the relation, and $f(1)=2+b=7$ gives $b=5$.
Thus $f(x)=2x+5$ and $f^{-1}(x)=\dfrac{x-5}{2}$ (its graph is the mirror image of $y=2x+5$ in $y=x$). Check: $f(x)+2f^{-1}(x)=2x+5+x-5=3x$.
originality_note: New: a relation between f and its inverse is turned, through x = f(t), into a relation for f o f, and a degree count forces f to be linear; the relation then leaves a one-parameter family fixed by f(1) = 7 (way 5). Closest known: finding f^{-1} of a given linear or Mobius function. Different because: neither f nor f^{-1} is given; both are recovered from one equation linking them.
stem_review: Read as a student: every set, function and symbol introduced with its domain, conditions complete, one reading of each sentence; answer recomputed with code and unique; answer matches the plan. Checked that the relation alone admits f(x) = x and the whole family 2x + b, so f(1) = 7 is needed and is sufficient; verified f(5) + f^{-1}(41) = 33 with sympy. Changed: No change.
key_step: Substituting x = f(t) to obtain f(f(t)) = 3f(t) - 2t, then the degree argument d^2 = d.
justification: Two linked ideas: using the inverse relation f^{-1}(f(t)) = t to remove the inverse, and a degree argument to force linearity, followed by coefficient matching with a case to reject. Above 2024-P2-Q8 (L2), a direct functional-equation evaluation; comparable to 2025-P2-Q14 (L3) on inverse functions.
blueprint_concepts: Inverse of a function: existence, graph symmetry about y = x
When a function and its inverse are both given

concept_use.Inverse of a function: existence, graph: Invertibility makes f onto, so x = f(t) can be substituted and f^{-1}(f(t)) = t; the graph of f^{-1}(x) = (x - 5)/2 is the reflection of y = 2x + 5 in y = x.
concept_use.When a function and its inverse are both: The given relation f(x) + 2f^{-1}(x) = 3x, linking a function and its inverse, is converted into f(f(t)) + 2t = 3f(t) and solved for f and f^{-1}.
